answer: Not automatically. The ISA has no standalone termination right triggered by Aldersgate's acquisition, even by a competitor. TerraNode's termination right arises only indirectly: (1) a change of control is treated as an assignment needing TerraNode's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld); (2) under the competitor carve-out, TerraNode may reasonably withhold consent if the acquirer or any Affiliate is a Direct Competitor (more than 15% of annual gross revenue from cloud infrastructure services); and (3) if the change of control then occurs without the required consent, TerraNode may give 30 days' written notice of termination, which does not take effect if Aldersgate obtains the required consent within 60 days of that notice. Whether the acquirer is a Direct Competitor, whether consent was sought and refused, and whether the deal closed without consent are all unresolved, so the right is conditional.

On the memo's expected October 15, 2025 closing, the premium would apply; a closing on or after November 1, 2025 would remove it. This is conditional on the actual closing date and the Loan principal prepaid.

answer: Yes, but only conditionally. Under §12.2, on a Change of Control of either party the other may terminate on 90 days' written notice. The right lapses only if the party undergoing the change gave at least 30 days' prior written notice of the anticipated Change of Control and the other party failed to deliver a written objection within that 30-day period. Silence therefore operates as deemed consent only when the advance notice is compliant. If the acquirer of Solara (Buyer) has annual revenues above $1 billion (or its ultimate parent does, if the acquirer is a subsidiary), §12.3 resets all Product pricing at closing to the lower of the then-current contract pricing and NovaBridge's Published Wholesale Schedule. This applies for the rest of the Term, including Renewal Terms. It is a price reset to the lower figure, not an increase, and the Minimum Purchase Commitment is unaffected. §12.3 applies only to a Change of Control of Buyer, so a change of control of NovaBridge would not trigger it.

answer: No. The permitted assignment to a merger successor in Section 16.1 does not eliminate the Customer's change-of-control termination right. Section 16.1 is expressly 'subject to, and shall not limit or modify' Customer's rights under Section 12.3. The right applies only if a 'Change of Control of Provider' occurred, meaning a transaction that changes more than 50% of Provider's voting equity or a sale of all or substantially all of its assets. Customer's termination notice must be 60 days' prior written notice.
